revision_scope: Uncommitted API changes over base_commit, bound by source/test hashes below; hosted CodeQL resolution is not claimed.

behavior.scope: both /api/checklists routes, shared per-client/per-process counter before JSON parsing or corpus I/O
behavior.headers: draft-8 RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy plus Retry-After for 429; exposed to allowed browser origins
behavior.log_format: constant first argument, client ID is a data argument

pre_fix.scope: Application export/listener test seam was present; rate middleware and constant log format were absent. No runtime/hook errors counted as regression evidence.

assertions.expected: RateLimit budget header present on a normal checklist response
Error logging first argument is constant Error fetching checklist %s:
assertions.observed: First argument interpolated the request ID; ERR_ASSERTION

checks: Normal listing and item reads expose shared remaining budget
100 requests exhaust one client budget across routes, including unknown IDs
Spoofed IPv4 and IPv6 forwarded headers cannot obtain a fresh budget
429 responses carry JSON, zero remaining budget and Retry-After
Exhausted client never reaches fs.access/readFile/readdir or JSON body parsing
Mocked clock advances beyond 60 seconds and next request is served with renewed budget
File-read errors keep the user-visible 500 envelope and log through a constant format string
Actual CLI process listens on documented port 3000 and serves the real corpus; test-only shutdown hook flushes real V8 counters
limitations: MemoryStore is process-local and resets on process restart; horizontal workers require a shared store before claiming deployment-wide rate enforcement
Hosted CodeQL alert state must be rechecked on the published revision
Clock-controlled local counter transitions are tested; no distributed simulation or deployment-wide attack-resistance claim

clock_scope: Node built-in MockTimers replaces Date only. Advancing it by 60,001 ms exercises request-time expiry of the real library memory store; HTTP and I/O run normally. This is a local counter transition check, not distributed simulation or a deployment-wide rate-limit claim.
